answer_1.quote: participants sought to write descriptions that could make images accessible to users who can't see them.
datasets: custom dataset of 54 image-context pairs (18 images, 17 Wikipedia articles)

answer_2.quote: We then use this experimental data to evaluate two very different referenceless metrics: CLIP-Score, which assesses a description's quality relative to its associated image, and SPURTS, which relies only on linguistic properties of the text.

answer_4.quote: Both groups can provide important insights. Sighted as well as BLV participants rated each image description as it occurred within the respective Wikipedia article.
answer_4.guideline: participants rated each description on five dimensions (Overall quality, Imaginability, Relevance, Irrelevance, Fit to the article) using 5-point Likert scales
